companion_apps.name: Anova Culinary
companion_apps.notes: Version 3.6.6 (versionCode 2127) was checked statically in the November 15 follow-up. Its React Native bundle contains all seven UUIDs in this spec and lacks the conflicting 96c3 clock spelling. That is UUID evidence only, not a claim that this app version was driven against a Mini.

identity.notes: The reference client keys a connection on the host Bluetooth device. Whether the Mini address is public or random and stable across resets is not established. SYSTEM_INFO contains a serial number, but it is private per-unit data: do not log, publish or commit it.

methods.notes: The official client compares advertised service UUIDs case-insensitively. Select by service first; an optional cooker_id is a case-sensitive name prefix supplied by the user, not protocol identity.

identification.notes: Require this advertised custom service, then verify all six characteristics after connecting. A local-name prefix may be used only as a secondary, user-supplied filter: the official client supports one, but no fixed Mini advertised name is established. Do not identify this cooker as an original Anova or Nano from its name alone.

device.name: Anova Precision Cooker Mini
device.notes:
The Mini speaks UTF-8 JSON wrapped in standard padded Base64 on six per-function characteristics. No Anova account, cloud API, fixed PIN, application key or provisioning credential appears in the official local client. Discovery uses the custom advertised service; an advertised name is optional and is not specified here.
STATE is both a readable state object and the destination for unit, start and stop objects. SET_TEMPERATURE and SET_CLOCK are separate destinations. Poll readable characteristics for the demonstrated client. The overview advertises notifications on four characteristics, but gives no subscription sequence or notification schema: do not assume notification bodies equal read bodies.
Every temperature number is in the cooker's CURRENT temperatureUnit, not in a unit carried by each command. Timer values in the demonstrated start object are integer seconds. Zero is the reference client's default timer, but its device-side meaning (disabled, unlimited or something else) is unknown and is not asserted here. The official reference always emits setpoint, timer, cookableId and cookableType for start; this spec does not invent behavior for omitted optional fields.
SCOPE: this is only the first Precision Cooker Mini documented by Anova's Mini-specific API. It is not the original Precision Cooker, Nano, A2/A3, Nano 3.0/Wi-Fi, or the later Mini/Lite family merely sharing a retail name.

openness.notes: The official pages are incomplete: no safe operating range, full state enumeration, notification schema, general timer-write object, universal error envelope or authenticated manual was recovered. This spec implements the demonstrated polling/command subset and leaves those questions open. It does not cover the original cooker's ASCII protocol, the Nano's COBS/protobuf protocol, later Mini/Lite hardware, Wi-Fi or Anova cloud APIs.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The Mini advertises its service without a documented button-only pairing window. Pairing is accepted at the host after connection. Use the top-button hold only for the documented recovery case.

exclusivity.notes: The official client establishes that pairing is required, but does not name the association model, bond capacity or connection limit. Calling it Just Works, numeric comparison or a fixed-PIN exchange would be an invention.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app and other centrals, then reconnect and accept the host pairing request. If pairing still fails, the official client's ten-second top-button recovery is the documented next step; its exact bond-clearing scope is unknown.

pairing.notes: Accepting the host pairing prompt is mandatory in the official Mini client. No application-layer pairing payload follows it. Actual reconnect behavior still needs a hardware check.

unpair.clears: Unknown. The top-button recovery permits pairing again, but the sources do not say whether it clears only the bond or additional settings.
unpair.notes: No standalone unpair procedure was found. Do not borrow the original cooker's Bluetooth-button behavior or assert that a full factory reset is required.

safety_advisory.detail: Use only a correctly installed cooker with the water and vessel conditions required by its own vendor instructions. No authentic Mini manual was acquired in the research, so this spec deliberately supplies no temperature range, water-depth rule or unattended-use claim. Read STATE for the current unit immediately before every setpoint or start write and again afterwards. An accepted ATT write is not proof that heating started, stopped or reached a safe condition: read STATE and CURRENT_TEMPERATURE, preserve unknown states, and keep stop_cooking available. The model-specific vendor manual, when obtained, takes precedence over this protocol reconstruction.
safety_advisory.summary: This spec can start and retarget an immersion heater. Starting a cook and changing its setpoint require a deliberate action; stopping remains an ordinary, immediately available command.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi passphrase, account token, application key or fixed pairing PIN is used by the documented local protocol.
stored_on_device: Bluetooth pairing state; exact storage and reset behavior are unknown

factory_reset.description: No complete Mini manual was recovered. The procedure below is a source-documented recovery action, not a claim of a fully understood factory reset, and it was not executed by this project.
factory_reset.effect: The official reference calls a ten-second top-button hold a reset that permits pairing again. It does not establish whether bonds, cook history, clock, unit or other settings are erased, nor whether every firmware revision behaves alike.

procedures.basis: Anova's Mini MIT reference client, scan-failure guidance at the pinned commit; not run against hardware.
procedures.indicator: The light turns off after the hold.
procedures.name: Top-button reset (scope not fully documented)

steps.action: Hold the Mini's top button for ten seconds until its light turns off.
Scan and pair again. Do not assume anything beyond the source's statement that this permits pairing again.

methods.description: Scan for the Mini service, connect, accept host pairing, verify all six characteristics, set the UTC clock and then poll state. Do not issue a heater write during setup.
methods.name: Direct BLE with host pairing

steps.action: Power the Mini and scan for advertisements carrying 910772a8-a5e7-49a7-bc6d-701e9a783a5c, then connect.
Accept the host's pairing request. Anova says the Mini disconnects if that request is not accepted; no fixed PIN is documented.
Discover the service and require SET_TEMPERATURE, CURRENT_TEMPERATURE, TIMER, STATE, SET_CLOCK and SYSTEM_INFO at the exact UUIDs in services before any command.
Write set_clock with the current UTC time and response required, then read STATE and record temperatureUnit before interpreting any temperature.
steps.expect: STATE decodes as a JSON object after strict Base64 and UTF-8 decoding; temperatureUnit is C or F. Do not substitute a temperature of zero for a failed read.

troubleshooting.fix: Close other clients. The official reference says to hold the top button for ten seconds until the light turns off, then retry. Its reset scope is unknown; see factory_reset and pairing.unpair rather than treating it as a proven full factory reset.
troubleshooting.symptom: The Mini does not appear or cannot be paired again.

setup.notes: There is no Wi-Fi provisioning or account setup in this BLE path. The official flow connects, accepts the host pairing request, verifies the GATT map and synchronizes the clock to UTC. It has not been replayed on hardware.

rejoin.notes: There is no router to rejoin on the BLE path. Moving hosts means pairing the new host and, only if needed, using the top-button recovery above. Whether the old bond must first be forgotten is not established.

testing.notes: No Mini was scanned, connected, paired or driven by this project. The protocol comes from Anova's Mini developer documentation and MIT reference client, exercised offline in the research pack. The unified Android app's React Native bundle corroborates the service and all six characteristics, including the 96e3 clock UUID, but not the command encoding or live model compatibility. Independent standard-library checks are in scripts/test_anova_precision_cooker_mini.py; their vectors are synthetic, not captures.

entities.name: Mini Sous Vide
entities.notes: STATE supplies the state object and current unit; no fixed unit or safe setpoint bounds are asserted. Start and setpoint are advanced commands. There is no generic turn_on binding: start_cooking requires setpoint, cookableId, cookableType and an explicit timer, and a no-argument action cannot supply them. A dedicated start action must gather every field. STATE's idle is the only established idle word; unknown states must not be displayed as stopped. Confirm turn_off by reading STATE.

entities.name: Mini Water Temperature
entities.notes: Decode payload_formats.CurrentTemperature and use STATE.temperatureUnit. Do not convert Fahrenheit a second time, and do not substitute zero when a read or decode fails.

entities.name: Mini Status
entities.notes: Text from State.state: only idle and cooking are documented; preserve all other values as unknown.

entities.name: Mini Temperature Unit
entities.notes: STATE.temperatureUnit C maps to option 0 and F to option 1. Read back after selection, then re-read the setpoint and water temperature in the new unit.

entities.name: Mini Timer Remaining
entities.notes: Integer remaining seconds from Timer. Timer.running says whether it is counting; no standalone timer setter is declared.

entities.name: Mini Firmware Version
entities.notes: SystemInfo.firmwareVersion. Do not expose SystemInfo.serialNumber as this entity or in logs.

evidence.app_static_analysis: The November 15 follow-up checked the sibling-held unified app com.anovaculinary.android 3.6.6 (versionCode 2127). All seven UUIDs in this spec occur in its React Native bundle; the conflicting 96c3 clock UUID does not. Only those identifier facts are used. No vendor symbol, private device identifier or unrecovered command payload is transcribed.

evidence.documentation_review: Anova's Mini overview, BLE protocol, API reference, commands and implementation pages were read in the November 1 research pack. The pinned MIT reference client supplied the exact GATT use, JSON/Base64 transport, response flags, command objects and two exact vectors. Offline research exercised those methods against fakes, not hardware. The recovered pages and source do not establish safe operating limits or a complete state/error model.
evidence.open_questions: See remaining_unknowns. First obtain an owner-authorized GATT and notification capture plus the authentic manual. Begin read-only, resolve the clock table, bond behavior and actual response/error shapes, then verify stop before any attended start or setpoint write.

CommandError.description: One documented error object, not a complete error catalogue or proof that all errors arrive on STATE.

fields.description: Machine-readable code. INVALID_TEMP is the only published example; invalid unit, wrong state, connection failure and timer range have no published codes.
fields.name: code

parse_rules: Surface error/code when present. Do not treat an arbitrary state value or an empty object as an error envelope.

CurrentTemperature.description: JSON object read from CURRENT_TEMPERATURE. The current number is already in State.temperatureUnit and needs no Base64-to-binary scaling.

fields.description: JSON number in the current device unit. Missing, null, non-numeric or malformed values are unknown and must not become zero.
fields.name: current

parse_rules: Apply the same strict Base64/UTF-8/JSON-object decoder as State, then require a finite numeric current before publishing a reading.

State.description: JSON object read from STATE after strict Base64 decoding. Published examples contain state and may contain temperatureUnit, currentTemperature and a timer object; tolerate additional or absent fields.

fields.description: String state. Only idle and cooking are documented; preserve all other values as unknown.
fields.name: state

fields.description: String C or F controlling every temperature in both directions. It is required before a setpoint write; an absent value is unknown, not a default C.
fields.name: temperatureUnit

fields.description: Optional JSON number in temperatureUnit. It is not substituted for a failed CURRENT_TEMPERATURE read.
fields.name: currentTemperature

fields.description: Optional object with boolean running and integer remaining seconds, matching Timer.
fields.name: timer

parse_rules: Strictly Base64-decode with standard alphabet and required padding, decode UTF-8, then require one JSON object; malformed data is an error, not {}.
Accept legal JSON whitespace and additional fields. Do not compare responses to one literal serialized string.
Preserve unknown state strings and missing fields. Only the exact documented idle value means idle.

SystemInfo.description: JSON object with deviceName, firmwareVersion and serialNumber plus possible additional fields.
parse_rules: Treat serialNumber as private per-unit identity. Use synthetic values in logs and test fixtures.

Timer.description: JSON object read from TIMER. Seconds are integer values, not milliseconds or minutes.

fields.description: Boolean countdown-running flag. Its post-completion behavior is undocumented.
fields.name: running

fields.description: Integer remaining seconds. No sentinel or post-completion value is documented.
fields.name: remaining

parse_rules: Require running to be a JSON boolean and remaining an integer when those fields are exposed; preserve additional fields.

command_steps: Construct exactly one command-specific JSON object with the declared field types.
Serialize the object as UTF-8 JSON. Ordinary JSON whitespace is not a protocol requirement; accept any legal whitespace on reads.
Apply standard Base64 with the normal alphabet and = padding to the complete UTF-8 byte sequence.
Write the Base64 ASCII bytes to the command's characteristic. SET_TEMPERATURE and STATE use write-without-response; SET_CLOCK uses write-with-response.
For reads, require the entire value to be valid padded Base64, then UTF-8, then one JSON object of the expected shape. Bound input sizes and distinguish malformed data from an actual empty object.
json_base64_transport.no_binary_envelope: No binary header, opcode, checksum, fixed-point conversion, terminator or application encryption layer is documented. Base64 is the outer encoding, not encryption. No MTU, maximum command length, long-write or fragmentation rule was recovered; do not invent a universal ATT limit from short examples.
json_base64_transport.polling_and_notifications: The demonstrated client polls STATE, CURRENT_TEMPERATURE, TIMER and SYSTEM_INFO. A full-state helper is three separate reads in that order, merging currentTemperature and timer into the state dictionary; it is not a device operation. Four characteristics advertise notify, but no subscription sequence or notification schema is public. Do not enable notifications and assume they carry these read objects without a capture.
json_base64_transport.write_result_is_not_device_state: A successful write or ATT acknowledgment is not evidence of heating, stopping, unit acceptance or reaching a setpoint. Read STATE after unit and cook writes and CURRENT_TEMPERATURE for bath progress. The reference client's interactive exit sends stop before disconnecting; that is an application choice, not proof that a bare disconnect stops the cooker.

source_conflicts.app_uuid_evidence: The November 15 verification found every Mini UUID in the unified app's React Native bundle. This supersedes the earlier research note's negative search only as a UUID finding. It does not prove command framing, current firmware support or a completed app-to-Mini connection.
source_conflicts.clock_uuid: Use d8a89692-cae8-4b74-96e3-0b99d3637793. The overview, API reference, pinned official client and unified app bundle agree; one BLE protocol page prints d8a89692-cae8-4b74-96c3-0b99d3637793, which was absent from that bundle. Hardware GATT discovery is still required to close the conflict.
source_conflicts.timer_write: TIMER is documented writable, but only start_cooking demonstrates setting a timer. No standalone TIMER write object is declared.

remaining_unknowns: The actual Mini GATT table and properties, including final resolution of the SET_CLOCK 96e3 versus 96c3 documentation conflict.
Authenticated manual limits: electrical ratings, safe temperature range, vessel/water requirements and regional-model differences. The reference client's example 65.0 is not a range.
The complete state enumeration and whether a distinct preheating/error state exists; unknown states must remain unknown.
Notification subscription requirements and payloads, including whether they equal the documented read objects.
Standalone SET_TEMPERATURE and TIMER read/write response schemas, timer zero semantics, completion behavior and valid timer bounds.
Error delivery and correlation beyond the single INVALID_TEMP example; invalid unit, wrong state, connection and timer errors have no published codes.
MTU, maximum command size, long-write and fragmentation behavior.
Pairing association model, central/bond limits, reconnect behavior, and exactly what the ten-second top-button reset clears.
Whether a bare disconnect leaves a cook running; only the reference interactive client's deliberate stop-on-exit is established.
Firmware update, Wi-Fi provisioning and unattended-heating behavior are outside this spec and unrecovered.

set_target_temperature.advanced_reason: Changing the target can heat an already-running bath, and a value interpreted in the wrong current unit can produce an unsafe cook. Read STATE first, confirm the unit and vessel conditions, then read STATE again afterwards. stop_cooking remains the recovery command.
set_target_temperature.description: Write the JSON object {"setpoint": <number>} using the current device unit, then apply the Base64 transport. The documented sequence sends this before start_cooking. No safe minimum or maximum was recovered, so the parameter deliberately has no range.

setpoint.description: A finite JSON number in the current STATE.temperatureUnit, without quotes or a unit suffix. The handler validates the number and emits no NaN or Infinity.

characteristics.name: SET_TEMPERATURE
characteristics.notes: The official client writes with response=False. The overview also calls this readable/notifiable, but does not document a standalone read or notification response schema. Only the write object below is declared.

characteristics.name: CURRENT_TEMPERATURE
characteristics.notes: Read and strictly decode Base64, UTF-8 and a JSON object with numeric current. The number is already in STATE.temperatureUnit: do not convert it a second time. A missing or malformed current is unknown, never 0.

characteristics.name: TIMER
characteristics.notes: The official client only reads this characteristic. Its demonstrated object has running and integer remaining seconds. The overview calls it writable, but no standalone timer-write object or completion semantics is documented; no write command is invented here.

set_temperature_unit.description: Write {"command":"changeUnit","payload":{"temperatureUnit":"C"}} or the F equivalent using the Base64 transport. UI parameter 0 maps to JSON C and 1 to JSON F. Read STATE afterwards to verify the new unit and re-read all temperatures; do not carry a numeric setpoint across the change unchanged.

unit.description: UI enum only: 0 becomes JSON string C; 1 becomes JSON string F.

start_cooking.advanced_reason: This can start an immersion heater. Confirm the current temperature unit, setpoint, timer and physical setup with the owner present, and keep stop_cooking immediately available. A write acknowledgment is not proof of heating; verify STATE and stop if it is unexpected.
start_cooking.description: Write the complete documented start object with setpoint, timer in integer seconds, cookableId and cookableType, using the Base64 transport. The reference emits all four payload fields even though its command page calls the last three optional. recipe123/recipe are offline example strings, not a real recipe or cloud lookup. Send set_target_temperature first for a timed cook and confirm the result through STATE rather than trusting the write result.

cookable_id.description: Opaque identifier emitted as cookableId. The official offline example value is recipe123, not a private or real recipe identifier; supply all four start fields as the reference does.

cookable_type.description: Opaque cookableType string. The official offline example value is recipe; supply it explicitly rather than inferring device-side omission behavior.

setpoint.description: Finite JSON number in the current STATE.temperatureUnit, with the same validation and lack of an asserted safe range as set_target_temperature.

timer.description: Non-negative integer seconds emitted in the start object. Zero is the reference default only; its device-side disabled/unlimited meaning is unknown. There is deliberately no automatic default: a dedicated action must gather the timer explicitly.

stop_cooking.description: Write {"command":"stop"} with response=False using the Base64 transport. This is the ordinary recovery path and is deliberately not advanced. Read STATE afterwards; a successful local write alone does not prove the heater stopped.

characteristics.name: STATE
characteristics.notes: Read the state object; write unit/start/stop objects with response=False. idle and cooking are the only published state words. Preserve every other state as unknown rather than mapping it to idle. Read this before and after every unit, setpoint and start write.

set_clock.description: Write {"currentTime":"2024-02-06T12:00:00+00:00"} with the actual current UTC time, Base64-encoded, using write-with-response. The command page also shows a trailing Z. Both forms are documented; accepted variants beyond those two are unknown. Microseconds are omitted in the reference client.

current_time.description: Current UTC ISO-8601 timestamp ending Z or +00:00, without fractional seconds. The client generates this at send time; never replay the example timestamp.

characteristics.name: SET_CLOCK
characteristics.notes: Write with response required. The overview, API reference, pinned client and current app bundle all support 96e3. One official BLE protocol page prints d8a89692-cae8-4b74-96c3-0b99d3637793 instead; that conflict is retained in remaining_unknowns pending a real GATT table. Do not probe the alternative by sending clock writes to an unidentified cooker.

characteristics.name: SYSTEM_INFO
characteristics.notes: Read a Base64/JSON object containing deviceName, firmwareVersion and serialNumber, with possible additional fields. Use an invented serial in fixtures and never publish a unit's real serial. Other services or a standard Battery Service may exist, but are not established here.

services.name: Anova Precision Cooker Mini control
services.notes: UUIDs and documented properties come from Anova's Mini overview and pinned client, with static UUID corroboration from the unified app. Command bodies are logical JSON objects: serialize as protocol_details.json_base64_transport specifies before writing. No notification payload schema is asserted.
